title: Readout-calibrated conditioned fermionic QKSD
difficulty_explanation: The solver must calibrate four asymmetric finite-shot Hadamard-test channels, reconstruct complex Hermitian Toeplitz QKSD matrices, filter an indefinite near-singular overlap before whitening, and reproduce phase-sensitive 56/60-mode Slater control moments through TensorCircuit's fermionic-Gaussian representation.
solution_explanation: The reference parses the raw calibration and signal counts, performs a prescribed noise-aware canonical orthogonalization, and uses TensorCircuit FGSSimulator evolution plus phase-preserving occupied-orbital determinants and transition-density linear solves for hidden control lags.
verification_explanation: The evaluator does not import TensorCircuit. It independently diagonalizes each hidden one-particle Hamiltonian, derives Slater determinants and Hamiltonian transition moments, generates seeded asymmetric-readout counts, repeats the complete conditioned QKSD pipeline, and checks a separate dense Jordan-Wigner Fock-space canary.
relevant_experience: The prototype combines quantum subspace diagonalization under finite sampling, measurement-error calibration, canonical orthogonalization of noisy overlap matrices, and phase-sensitive fermionic-Gaussian transition formulas.

contract.anti_hardcoding: The seed changes mode count, hidden relabeling, onsite disorder, complex Peierls phases, occupied modes, readout responses, calibration counts, all signal counts, and nonces; exact control moments and final Ritz values are never included in the configuration.
contract.oracle: Independent complex128 one-particle evolution and Slater transition determinants, seeded binomial readout channels, full QKSD reconstruction, and a separate 16-dimensional Jordan-Wigner Fock-space canary

difficulty_levers: 56- and 60-mode production cases rule out dense qubit statevectors
complex hopping phases make magnitude-only Gaussian overlaps fail
four independently calibrated asymmetric binary readout channels
shot noise deliberately makes the sampled overlap indefinite
canonical filtering and whitening at a seed-stable noise cutoff
both sampled Ritz outputs and noiseless extrapolation controls are scored
claim_boundary: This is a deterministic synthetic finite-shot QKSD benchmark with a declared sector-normalized Hadamard-test model. It does not model coherent gate error or claim hardware-level performance. No solver-model trial has been run and no model-hardness claim is made.
numerical_statistical_risks: Finite calibration counts perturb both the readout slope and offset; calibration noise is intentionally propagated rather than treated as known exactly.
Independent quadrature sampling breaks Toeplitz positive semidefiniteness before explicit Hermitization and filtering.
An overlap eigenvalue close to the cutoff could make retained rank seed-sensitive; validation therefore checks multiple seeds and requires a visible cutoff margin.
Slater transition determinants can be small, so Hamiltonian transition moments use complex128 linear solves instead of explicit inverses.
Shot-derived Ritz energies are estimators and need not be variational upper bounds after overlap filtering.
api_risks: FGSSimulator.evol_hamiltonian applies exp(-i h) to the 2L by L alpha representation; the number-conserving particle/hole block and time-step convention must be canaried after upgrades.
FGSSimulator.overlap returns a nonnegative magnitude in the pinned release and cannot supply the U(1) phase required here.
The occupied orbitals are recovered from the lower alpha block under the pinned particle-hole convention; a representation change would alter control phases.
TensorCircuit backend and dtype setters are process-global, so the expert explicitly selects NumPy and complex128.
